title: STAT+: Lobbyists and trade groups fight to shape how states regulate medical AI
key_facts: A 22-member AI workgroup convened by the Federation of State Medical Boards (FSMB) met behind closed doors in Washington in early October.
Members include executives from the American Medical Association, the American Hospital Association, Anthropic and the insurer Elevance Health, plus state government representatives.
Goal: draft guidelines for state medical boards on AI in the practice of medicine, with attention to tools that perform clinical functions with limited or no direct physician supervision.
Discussions are confidential; a draft could be public in 'weeks to months', FSMB president and CEO Humayun Chaudhry told STAT.
Guidelines could ultimately form the basis of state legislation; recommendations will be open for feedback before adoption.
quote_evidence: Executives from the American Medical Association, American Hospital Association, artificial intelligence giant Anthropic, and insurer Elevance Health are part of a 22 member AI workgroup convened by the Federation of State Medical Boards.
A draft of the recommendations could be made public in “weeks to months,” said Chaudhry.
why_it_matters_hint: State medical boards decide who may practise medicine, so guidelines written here could shape how autonomous medical AI is allowed to work.
notes: Only the free intro of a STAT+ article was available (about 2,200 characters), so detail beyond that is not covered.
